lessons.title: Invite to the Oneness First
lessons.intro: Learn what the Prophet ﷺ told Mu’adh to begin with when he sent him to Yemen, how a letter to a king began, and how to start a conversation about Islam with Allah, not with rules.

steps.title: What is da’wah?
body: Da’wah means invitation. A Muslim who shares Islam is inviting, not forcing, and not winning an argument. The Qur’an tells the Prophet ﷺ to invite to the way of his Lord (16:125).
Anyone can invite. A parent, a classmate or a neighbour can share what they know and live by. This course is about how to do it well.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The order given to Mu’adh
body: When the Prophet ﷺ sent Mu’adh to Yemen, he told him what to invite people to first: to testify that none has the right to be worshipped but Allah and that he is Allah’s Messenger. If they obey in that, then teach them that Allah has made five prayers obligatory every day and night. If they obey in that, then teach them that Allah has made zakat obligatory, taken from their rich and given to their poor (Bukhari 1395).
The order matters. The first call is to Allah. Laws come after.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The first thing
steps.note: This is the first part of the testimony. The call begins here.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A letter to a king
body: The Prophet ﷺ also wrote letters to rulers. In the letter to Heraclius, the ruler of the Byzantines, he began with peace on the one who follows the right path, then invited him to Islam. The letter quoted an ayah: come to a word common between us, that we worship none but Allah and associate nothing with Him, and that none of us takes others as lords instead of Allah (3:64; Bukhari 7).
The letter did not begin with a list of rules. It began with Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Teaching the Qur’an in Madinah
body: Al-Bara ibn Azib reported that the first people who came to Madinah before the Prophet ﷺ were Mus’ab ibn Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum, and they were teaching the Qur’an to the people (Bukhari 3925).
This is a good model. Share the Qur’an, and share what you live by.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The older lesson text said Mus’ab was sent with “the shahada”; Bukhari 3925 says he taught the Qur’an. The text now follows the hadith.

steps.title: Why start with Allah?
body: Rules make sense only if you know who gives them. A person who is asked to follow rules before knowing Allah may feel only a burden. A person who knows Allah’s mercy and oneness is more likely to want to know what He asks.
This is not a rule from a text. It is a lesson from the way the Prophet ﷺ ordered the invitation.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Starting a conversation about Islam

steps.detail: Ask what they already believe. You may find common ground.
Talk about His oneness and mercy before any rules.
A single ayah or a single story is enough.
Avoid jargon.
Say they are welcome to ask anything later.

mistakes: Starting with a list of dos and don’ts.
Talking more than listening.

steps.review: Practical guidance worded by the app author. Please confirm.

lessons.title: Wisdom Is Knowing the Person
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an means by wisdom and good instruction, how the Prophet ﷺ answered different people, and how to prepare for a conversation by thinking about the person.

steps.title: The ayah of invitation
steps.note: Read it one word at a time. The ayah gives three ways to invite: with wisdom, with good instruction, and by arguing in the best way.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Three doors
body: The ayah names three ways to invite. Wisdom (hikmah) is knowing what to say, how and when. Good instruction (mau’izah hasanah) is advice given with care. Argument in the best way (jidal) is for when there is a disagreement, and it must be done in the best manner.
The end of the ayah says that your Lord knows best who has strayed and who is guided. You are not the judge.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The explanation of the three terms is a common summary. Please confirm the wording.

steps.title: Different answers to different people
body: In one report, the Prophet ﷺ was asked which deed is the best, and he answered belief in Allah and His Messenger, then jihad, then an accepted Hajj (Bukhari 26). In another, Abdullah ibn Mas’ud asked which deed is dearest to Allah, and he answered prayer at its time, then kindness to parents, then jihad (Bukhari 527).
Scholars explain such differences as the Prophet ﷺ answering what suited the person or the time. This is an explanation, not stated in the hadith.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The reports are verbatim from the corpus. The explanation that the answers suit the person or time is a common scholarly reading but not in the hadith text; please confirm.

steps.title: The man in the mosque
body: A Bedouin stood up and began to urinate in the mosque. The people caught him, but the Prophet ﷺ told them to leave him, and had a bucket of water poured over the place. Then he said: you were sent to make things easy, not difficult (Bukhari 220).
The man did not yet know the manners of the mosque. He was taught gently.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Know the person
body: Wisdom begins with the person in front of you. A student, an older neighbour and a worried parent each carry something different. Ask what they are carrying today.
The message is one. The door is tailored.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Before a conversation

steps.text: Spend two minutes thinking about the person.
steps.detail: What are they going through? What do they care about?
Choose something that fits them.
Gentle, clear and short.
Ask Allah to put the right words in your mouth.
Questions are better than speeches.

mistakes: Using the same speech for everyone.
Arguing to win.

lessons.title: The Ta’if Standard
lessons.intro: Learn the hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ was offered revenge on those who rejected him and chose hope for their children instead, and what this means when someone mocks your faith.

steps.title: The hardest day
body: Aisha asked the Prophet ﷺ: have you faced a day harder than the day of Uhud? He said: your people troubled me a lot, and the worst was the day of Aqaba, when I presented myself to Ibn Abd Yalil, and he did not respond.

The Prophet ﷺ left overwhelmed with sorrow and did not recover until he was at Qarn ath-Tha’alib. There he lifted his head and saw a cloud giving him shade, and Jibril was in it. Jibril said that Allah had heard what the people said to him and sent the Angel of the Mountains to do whatever he wished.

The Angel of the Mountains greeted him and said: order what you wish. If you like, I will let the two mountains fall on them. The Prophet ﷺ said: no, I hope that Allah will bring from their descendants those who worship Allah alone, associating nothing with Him (Bukhari 3231).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the hadith says and what it does not
body: Many biographies connect the day of Aqaba in this hadith with the Prophet’s visit to Ta’if. The hadith does not use the name Ta’if, and it does not mention stones or blood. Those details come from the biographers (the seerah), and this lesson does not repeat them as part of the hadith.
What the hadith does tell us is clear and enough: he was refused, he was offered revenge, and he said no.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The link of the day of Aqaba to Ta’if and the stoning story are seerah reports that this app has not verified against a hadith collection. The lesson says so. Please confirm the wording.

steps.title: A prayer for those who refuse
steps.note: When Tufayl and his companions asked the Prophet ﷺ to pray against the tribe of Daus, he prayed for their guidance instead.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The pattern
body: In both reports, the Prophet ﷺ had the chance to ask for harm to his opponents, and chose hope for them instead. The Qur’an teaches the same: the good deed and the bad are not equal, so repel evil with what is better, and the one who was an enemy may become a close friend (41:34).
It also says that it was by mercy from Allah that he was gentle with them, and that if he had been harsh, they would have left (3:159).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Repel with what is better
steps.note: Read slowly. The ayah is a plan: do what is better, and see the change.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: When someone mocks your faith
steps.intro: A few steps for a moment that stings.

steps.text: Take a breath before you answer.
steps.detail: You do not owe an instant reply.
It makes the other person defend, not listen.

steps.text: Answer calmly with one true sentence.
steps.detail: For example: it matters to me, and I am happy to explain if you want.
The Prophet ﷺ prayed for guidance for Daus.

steps.text: Walk away if it turns into abuse.
steps.detail: You do not have to stay in a place that harms you.

mistakes: Replying with an insult.
Staying in a conversation that has turned abusive.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Practical guidance worded by the app author. Please confirm.

lessons.title: Your Life Is the Loudest Sermon
lessons.intro: Learn how the people around the Prophet ﷺ knew him as truthful before they heard his message, and how your own character opens or closes the door.

steps.title: Standing on Safa
body: When the ayah to warn his closest relatives was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ climbed Safa and called the tribes of Quraysh. He asked: if I told you that there was a cavalry in the valley about to attack, would you believe me? They said: yes, we have never found you telling anything but the truth. Then he said that he was a warner of a severe punishment (Bukhari 4770).
Their trust in his honesty came before they heard his message.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Khadija’s words
body: After the first revelation, the Prophet ﷺ came home afraid. Khadija told him: never, by Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You keep good relations with your kin, help the poor and destitute, serve your guests generously and help those hit by calamity (Bukhari 3).
She named his character as the reason for her trust.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Even an opponent noticed
body: Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan whether the Prophet ﷺ had been accused of lying before his claim. Abu Sufyan said no. Heraclius said: I wondered how a person who does not lie about people could lie about Allah (Bukhari 7).
Biographers also report that his people called him al-Amin, the trustworthy. This app has not checked that title against a hadith collection, so it is not used as a proof here.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The al-Amin title is a seerah report that has not been verified against a hadith collection. The lesson says so. Please confirm.

steps.title: The religion is sincere care
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ said this to his Companions, who asked: to whom? He said: to Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, and to the leaders of the Muslims and their common people.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Say what you do
body: The Qur’an warns believers: why do you say what you do not do? It is greatly hateful to Allah that you say what you do not do (61:2-3).
It does not mean you must be perfect before you speak. It means that what you say and what you do should match as far as you can.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The second sentence is the app author’s explanation. Please confirm.

steps.title: Convey from me
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ told people to convey from him, even one ayah. You do not have to know everything.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Calling to good
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like those who follow it, without their rewards being reduced at all (Muslim 2674).
A hadith like this should make us humble and careful, not proud. We invite because Allah loves it, not to be seen.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.text: Ask: does my behaviour open or close the door?
steps.detail: Be honest.
For example punctuality, a promise, or the way you speak when angry.
A small apology often opens a closed door.
Character is a gift to ask for.

Using your character as a reason to stay quiet.

lessons.title: Why Do Bad Things Happen?
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith say about hardship, and how to answer, and sit with, a person who asks this question in pain.

steps.title: The question behind the question
body: When someone asks why bad things happen, they are often not asking for a lecture. They may be grieving, scared or angry. The first thing to offer is presence and care.
The Qur’an does give answers, and they are worth knowing. Offer them gently and in small pieces.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Life as a test
steps.note: The ayah says Allah created death and life to test which of you is best in deed. Notice that it ends with two names: the Exalted in Might and the Forgiving.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the Qur’an says about hardship
body: Allah says that He will test people with fear, hunger, loss of wealth, lives and fruits, and gives good news to the patient, who say when disaster strikes: we belong to Allah and to Him we return (2:155-156).
It also says that perhaps you dislike something and it is good for you, and perhaps you love something and it is bad for you, and that Allah knows while you do not (2:216).
Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity (2:286), and with hardship there is ease (94:5-6).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: With hardship is ease
steps.note: Say both ayat. They repeat the same promise. Notice the word with: the ease comes with the hardship, not only after it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the hadith adds
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that no fatigue, illness, sorrow, sadness, harm or distress befalls a Muslim, even a thorn’s prick, but that Allah expiates some of his sins for it (Bukhari 5641).

He also said how wonderful the affair of the believer is: all of it is good. If good times reach him he is thankful, and that is good for him. If hardship reaches him he is patient, and that is good for him (Muslim 2999).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The affair of the believer
steps.note: Say it in parts. It gives two responses to two kinds of days: thanks and patience.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What we do not know
body: We can say that Allah is wise and just, and that He is merciful. We cannot always say why a particular thing happened to a particular person. It is better to admit this than to guess.
It is also wrong to tell a grieving person that their hardship was a punishment. We do not know that.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Guidance worded by the app author on how to speak about hardship. Please confirm that it is consistent with the Sunni teaching.

steps.text: Encourage help if they are in danger.

lessons.title: Islam Is Too Strict
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an and hadith say about ease, how the Prophet ﷺ chose the easier way, and how to speak about rules with mercy and honesty.

steps.title: A common worry
body: Some people feel Islam has too many rules. Others have been shown only the strictest side. It helps to know what the sources say about ease.
The Qur’an says Allah intends ease for you and does not intend hardship (2:185), and that He has not placed any difficulty on you in the religion (22:78).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: As much as you are able
steps.note: The ayah says to be mindful of Allah as much as you are able. Notice the phrase that sets the limit: as much as you are able.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Make things easy
steps.note: The Prophet ﷺ gave two pairs: make it easy and do not make it hard; give good news and do not drive people away.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: He chose the easier way
body: Aisha said that whenever the Prophet ﷺ was given a choice between two matters, he chose the easier one as long as it was not a sin. If it was a sin, he kept furthest from it (Bukhari 6126).
He also said the religion is easy, and whoever overburdens himself in it will not be able to continue. So do not go to extremes, aim to be near the mark, and take heart (Bukhari 39).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Ease is not the same as dropping what is required
body: Ease does not mean that anything can be changed. Prayer, fasting and the other obligations remain. Ease means that Allah gave concessions where there is hardship: for example the sick and the traveller may delay or shorten some acts (2:185).
And when you describe Islam, you can say that the rules exist. Hiding them is not honest. What you can do is to put mercy and ease first.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The first paragraph is a general summary of how ease works within obligations. Please confirm that it is stated correctly.

steps.title: The floor and the ceiling
body: It can help to explain that Islam has a floor: what Allah requires. Above that is a wide space of encouraged acts that no one is forced into. A new Muslim can start with the floor.
This is an image, not a ruling.

lessons.title: The Qur’an Was Written by a Man
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an itself says in answer to this claim: the challenge to produce something like it, the Prophet’s own background, and the passages that go against his own interest.

steps.title: The claim
body: Some people say that Muhammad ﷺ wrote the Qur’an himself. The Qur’an mentions this claim and answers it. This lesson shows what the Qur’an says. You are not expected to prove it to anyone. You are expected to understand the answer.
Muslims believe the Qur’an is the word of Allah. These are the reasons the Qur’an itself offers.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The challenge
body: The Qur’an challenges its doubters. It says that if mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of it, they could not (17:88). It then asks them to bring ten surahs like it (11:13), and then one surah (10:38; 2:23).
Scholars often describe this as a ladder that gets easier at each step. The challenge is set in Arabic, to the people who were the best in Arabic at that time.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The description of the challenge as a ladder and its audience is a common summary. Please confirm the wording.

steps.title: One surah like it
steps.note: Read one word at a time. Notice the ending: if you are truthful.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: He was not a writer of scripture
body: The Qur’an says that he did not recite or write any scripture before it, otherwise those who falsify would have had cause for doubt (29:48). It also says that he did not know what the Book or faith was before the revelation (42:52).
These are statements within the Qur’an. They fit the hadith in which the angel asked him to read and he said: I do not know how to read (Bukhari 3).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A book that corrects its own messenger
body: Surah Abasa begins by saying that the Prophet frowned and turned away because a blind man came to him (80:1-2). It continues with a correction (80:3-10). A person who made up a book might not include a passage that corrects himself.
This is an argument that people make. It is offered for reflection.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The argument from self-correction is a commonly made argument, not a ruling. Please confirm that it is stated fairly.

steps.title: Jubayr hears At-Tur
body: Jubayr ibn Mut’im, who was not yet Muslim, heard the Prophet ﷺ recite Surah At-Tur in the Maghrib prayer. When the recitation reached the ayat that ask whether they were created from nothing, or whether they are the creators, or whether they created the heavens and the earth, he said his heart was about to fly (Bukhari 4854).
He later became a Muslim. The report tells us how the Qur’an affected someone who was listening.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The last sentence is the biographers’ report that Jubayr later became Muslim; it is well known but not in this hadith. Please confirm.

lessons.title: I Have Done Too Much Wrong
lessons.intro: Learn the ayah for the person who thinks they are too far gone, the hadith of the man who killed ninety-nine, and how to answer someone who confesses a sin.

steps.title: The ayah of hope
steps.note: Read one word at a time. It begins with Say, and then speaks to those who have transgressed against themselves.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Do not despair
body: The ayah is addressed to people who have wronged themselves. It tells them not to despair of Allah’s mercy, and it says that Allah forgives all sins, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful (39:53).
This is the verse to give first to someone who feels too far gone.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The man who killed ninety-nine
body: The Prophet ﷺ told of a man from the Children of Israel who had killed ninety-nine people. He asked a monk if he could be forgiven. The monk said no, and he killed him too. He kept asking, and someone told him to go to a certain village. He died on the way, and the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed over him. Allah told the two lands to measure, and the man was nearer to the village he was heading for, so the angels of mercy took him (Bukhari 3470).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Repentance is welcomed
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than a man who lost his animal with his food and drink in the desert and then finds it (Bukhari 6308; Muslim 2744).
He also said that a believer sees his sins as if he were under a mountain that might fall on him. That fear is a sign of life in the heart (Bukhari 6308).
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The last sentence about fear being a sign of life is the app author’s reflection. Please confirm.

steps.title: Sins as great as the earth
body: Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said Allah says: son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me, I forgive you whatever you have done. If your sins reached the clouds and you asked forgiveness, I would forgive you. If you came with sins nearly as great as the earth, then met Me without associating anything with Me, I would come with forgiveness nearly as great as it (Tirmidhi 3540, graded sahih by Shakir and al-Albani, hasan by Bashar Awad Maarouf, and isnaad hasan by Zubair Ali Zai).
The graders agree it is acceptable. They differ on the level. It is a hadith that scholars use for hope, with the condition that the person meets Allah without shirk.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.source: Tirmidhi 3540 (graded sahih by Shakir and al-Albani; hasan by Bashar Awad Maarouf; isnaad hasan by Zubair Ali Zai)

steps.title: Islam wipes out what came before
body: Amr ibn al-As came to the Prophet ﷺ to pledge allegiance but wished to set a condition: that he be forgiven. The Prophet ﷺ said: do you not know that Islam wipes out what came before it? (Muslim 121).
This is for someone coming to Islam. For a Muslim who sins, the way is sincere repentance.
steps.label: [Established]
steps.review: The second paragraph is a general summary that sincere repentance is the way for a Muslim. Please confirm.

steps.detail: If they talk of harming themselves, stay with them and help them contact a doctor or emergency service.

mistakes: Giving a speech about the sin before showing hope.

lessons.title: Gentleness Does Not Water Down the Truth
lessons.intro: Learn why the Prophet ﷺ praised gentleness, how Musa was told to speak to Pharaoh, and how to stay gentle while saying what is true.

steps.title: A hadith on gentleness
steps.note: Say it in two parts. The first part is about what gentleness adds. The second is about what happens when it is taken away.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Gentleness adds beauty
body: Aisha reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: kindness is not found in anything but it adds to its beauty, and it is not taken away from anything but it makes it defective (Muslim 2594).
Gentleness is not weakness, and it does not change the message. It changes how the message reaches the heart.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Musa and Pharaoh
body: Allah sent Musa and Harun to Pharaoh and described him as one who had transgressed (20:43). Yet He told them to speak to him with gentle speech, so that perhaps he might be reminded or fear (20:44).
If gentle speech was asked for with Pharaoh, it is asked of us with those who disagree with us.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Gentle speech
steps.note: Read slowly. The phrase qawlan layyinan means gentle speech.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Aisha and the greeting
body: A group of Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: as-samu alaykum, which means death be upon you. Aisha understood it and replied: and upon you be death and the curse. The Prophet ﷺ said: be calm, Aisha. Allah loves gentleness in all matters. She said: did you not hear what they said? He said that he had already replied: and upon you (Bukhari 6024).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Gentle does not mean diluted
body: Musa was gentle, and he still told Pharaoh the truth. The Prophet ﷺ was gentle, and he still told his people what Allah had revealed.
You can lower your voice without lowering the message. The volume is not the proof.

lessons.title: Knowledge Before Speech
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an says about speaking without knowledge, what the Prophet ﷺ said about how knowledge leaves the world, and what to say when you do not know.

steps.title: Do not say what you do not know
body: The Qur’an says that Allah forbade immorality, sin, wrongdoing, associating others with Him, and that you say about Allah what you do not know (7:33).
It also tells us not to pursue what we have no knowledge of, because hearing, sight and the heart will be questioned (17:36).
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Do not pursue what you do not know
steps.note: Read slowly. The ayah ends by saying that the hearing, sight and heart will all be asked.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: How knowledge leaves
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that Allah does not take knowledge away by pulling it from people’s hearts. He takes it away by taking the scholars, until none remain. Then people take ignorant leaders, who are asked and give rulings without knowledge. They go astray and lead others astray (Bukhari 100).
This is a warning for all of us: when we are asked, we should not answer beyond what we know.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Musa and the question of who knows most
body: The Prophet ﷺ told of Musa addressing the Children of Israel. He was asked who the most knowledgeable person was, and he said: I am. Allah corrected him, because he had not attributed knowledge to Allah, and told him of a servant at the meeting of the two seas who knew more (Bukhari 122).
Even a prophet was corrected for not returning knowledge to Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: It is fine to say: I do not know
body: Saying I do not know is not a failure. It is honest, and it protects the other person from a wrong answer. You can say: that is a good question, let me find out and come back to you.
Then find out from a reliable source: a teacher, a trusted book, or an app that shows its sources.

lessons.title: Release the Result
lessons.intro: Learn what the Qur’an says about the Prophet’s job and what was not his job, and how to deliver a message and leave the outcome with Allah.

steps.title: You are a reminder
steps.note: Two short ayat that describe the job. Notice the word mudhakkir, one who reminds, and the word musaytir, one who controls.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The job and what is not the job
body: The Qur’an tells the Prophet ﷺ that he is only a reminder, not a controller over them (88:21-22). It says that only clear notification is upon him if they turn away (16:82), that he does not guide whom he likes but Allah guides whom He wills (28:56), and that their guidance is not upon him (2:272).
The job is to deliver clearly, kindly and honestly. The heart that opens is Allah’s to open.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: His uncle
body: When Abu Talib was dying, the Prophet ﷺ went to him and found Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya with him. He said: uncle, say there is no god but Allah, a word I will argue for you with before Allah. The two kept saying: would you leave the religion of Abd al-Muttalib? Abu Talib’s last words were that he was on the religion of Abd al-Muttalib, and he refused to say it (Bukhari 1360; Muslim 24).

The report then says that the ayah was revealed telling the Prophet ﷺ that he does not guide whom he loves, but Allah guides whom He wills (Muslim 24; Qur’an 28:56). The Prophet ﷺ loved his uncle and still could not make his heart open.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Prophets with few followers
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that the nations were shown to him. A prophet passed with one man, another with two, another with a group, and another with nobody (Bukhari 5752).
Some prophets delivered their message faithfully and had no followers. That did not make them less of a prophet. Success is not measured by how many followed.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What this gives you
body: If you think you are responsible for the result, every refusal feels like a failure. If you know your job is to deliver, you can speak with calm and then rest.
It does not mean you stop caring. The Qur’an describes the Prophet’s concern for people (9:128). It means you leave the outcome to Allah.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.text: Ask yourself: did I deliver clearly, kindly and honestly?
steps.detail: That is your job.

steps.text: Say quietly: I delivered it; You guide the hearts.
steps.detail: Then let it go.

steps.text: Do not follow up with pressure.
steps.detail: Be available if they come back.

steps.text: Carry on being a good neighbour.
steps.detail: Your kindness continues the message.

options.reteach: He refused to say it.
He said he was on the religion of Abd al-Muttalib.

items.q: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about some prophets?

options.reteach: The hadith says some had none.
The hadith says some had one or two.

options.text: Some passed with only one man, and some with nobody

items.q: What is your job in da’wah?

options.reteach: That is not in your control.

options.text: To deliver clearly, kindly and honestly

options.reteach: The job is to deliver.

items.explain: The heart is Allah’s to open.

items.q: Which word means “a reminder” in 88:21?

options.reteach: That is anta, “you are”.
That is fa-dhakkir, “so remind”.

items.q: What does this lesson suggest?

options.text: Keep pressing him until he agrees
options.reteach: Your job is to deliver.

options.text: You delivered. Make a dua for him, stay kind, and leave the result with Allah.

options.reteach: Stay kind and available.

items.scenario: You shared your faith with a close friend, and he did not accept. You feel you failed.

steps.title: Read Surah Al-Ghashiyah
steps.body: Open Surah Al-Ghashiyah and read the last ayat. Read their meaning.

canDo: Say what your job is in da’wah
Say what is not your job
Tell the report of Abu Talib and what the ayah says
Finish a conversation with a dua and without pressure
